# Walkthrough

This chapter builds a small fleet from scratch, start to finish.

You will create a new database and add four pickup trucks sharing a Template, one generator with its own one-off Schedule, a mix of in-house and outside service, and a closing report.

Start from a fresh, empty database: **New Database** on the Home screen, Blank Database, any Company Name you like. This walkthrough's own database used these settings:

![](assets/wt-db-details.png){width=60%}

## 1. Create an Asset Type

Service screen → Templates tab. A brand new database starts here: no Asset Types, nothing to select yet.

![](assets/wt-service-templates-empty.png)

Asset Type dropdown → **+ Create New Asset Type…**

- Name: `Pickup Truck`
- Usage Type: `Miles`

![](assets/wt-asset-type.png){width=60%}

## 2. Create Two Service Types

Still on the Templates tab, with Pickup Truck selected → **+ Add Rule**, twice.

![](assets/wt-add-rule.png){width=60%}

**Oil Change:**

- Service Type: **+ New Service Type…** → `Oil Change`
- Usage Interval: `5000`
- Time Interval: `6` `Months`

![](assets/wt-add-rule-oil-change.png){width=60%}

**Tire Rotation:**

- Service Type: **+ New Service Type…** → `Tire Rotation`
- Usage Interval: `6000`

![](assets/wt-templates.png)

## 3. Build the Fleet

Fleet screen → **+ Add Asset**, four times, Asset Type `Pickup Truck` each time:

| Name    | Make | Model | Year |
|---------|------|-------|------|
| Truck A | Ford | F-150 | 2022 |
| Truck B | Ford | F-150 | 2022 |
| Truck C | Ford | F-150 | 2022 |
| Truck D | Ford | F-150 | 2022 |

![](assets/wt-add-asset-truck-a.png){width=60%}

Each truck's Schedule tab now shows both Oil Change and Tire Rotation, copied from the Template.

Then **+ Add Asset** once more, creating a second Asset Type inline:

- Name: `Generator A`
- Asset Type: **+ Create New Asset Type…** → Name: `Generator`, Usage Type: `Hours`
- Make: `Generac Mobile`, Model: `MMG45`, Fuel Type: `Diesel`

![](assets/wt-add-asset-generator.png){width=60%}

Generator A's Schedule tab is empty because Generator has no Template yet.

## 4. Give Generator A Its Own Schedule

Fleet → Generator A → Schedule tab → **+ Add Schedule Item**

- Service Type: `Oil Change`
- Usage Interval: `250`

![](assets/wt-add-schedule-item.png){width=60%}

This is the zero-Template case from [Fleet](fleet.qmd#schedule-tab): Generator A gets a schedule item directly, with no type-level Template behind it.

![](assets/wt-fleet-built.png)

## 5. Log Service Events

Seven events, spread over the last two months, mixing in-house work with one outside shop.

First, from any Log Service dialog, create the shop and its technician once (**+** next to Company, then **+** next to Technician):

![](assets/wt-log-service-empty.png){width=60%}

- Company: `Shop A` (leave *Internal (In-House)* unchecked)

![](assets/wt-new-company.png){width=60%}

- Technician: `Jack` `Hass` `Wrench`, Company `Shop A`

![](assets/wt-new-technician.png){width=60%}

![](assets/wt-log-service.png){width=60%}

Then, Fleet → each asset → **Log Service**:

| Asset       | Service       | Company | Technician       | Date         | Usage        | Cost |
|-------------|---------------|---------|-------------------|--------------|--------------|------|
| Truck A     | Oil Change    | In-house| --                | 2 months ago | 11,200 mi    | $45  |
| Truck B     | Oil Change    | In-house| --                | 2 months ago | 9,800 mi     | $45  |
| Truck C     | Oil Change    | Shop A  | Jack Hass Wrench  | 1 month ago  | 14,300 mi    | $85  |
| Truck A     | Tire Rotation | In-house| --                | 1 month ago  | 11,950 mi    | $25  |
| Truck D     | Oil Change    | In-house| --                | today        | 6,500 mi     | $45  |
| Generator A | Oil Change    | In-house| --                | today        | 180 hr       | $70  |
| Truck B     | Tire Rotation | Shop A  | Jack Hass Wrench  | today        | 10,200 mi    | $55  |

![](assets/wt-service-log.png)

## 6. Log Usage on One Asset

Fleet → Truck A → **Log Usage**, twice:

| Date         | Reading    | Fuel Qty | Fuel Cost |
|--------------|------------|----------|-----------|
| 1 month ago  | 12,000 mi  | 16 gal   | $60       |
| today        | 12,400 mi  | 18 gal   | $65       |

![](assets/wt-log-usage.png){width=60%}

Two entries, not one -- Economy needs a delta between two readings to compute anything (see [Fleet](fleet.qmd#usage-tab)).

![](assets/wt-asset-usage.png)

## 7. Check the Dashboard

Dashboard → Summary tab. Seven events, both companies, three months of spend -- enough for every chart to show something real.

![](assets/wt-dashboard-summary.png)

## 8. Export a Report

Reports → Service History tab → Export → **Export PDF**.

![](assets/wt-reports-service-history.png)

Compare your export against a [reference PDF](data/walkthrough-service-history.pdf) generated from this exact walkthrough. See if you get the same seven events, same $370.00 total.

That's a complete cycle:

- An Asset Type and its Templates
- A fleet built against them
- A one-off Schedule item for an asset with no Template
- Service history across two companies
- Usage tracking
- A real, exported document
